text.p: Italian debt markets sunk, pulled down by own their weight in late trade as a vacuum of buying interest let prices spiral lower in the course of the day.

Brokers said investors had simply withdrawn their hands from the game as they waited for more clarification about the prospects for European monetary union and for signals on the prospects for an effective Italian minibudget.

"The market is weak. Italian economic fundamentals are good but we have to pay for political uncertainty and EMU uncertainty," one broker at a London bank said. The lira was looking sickly at 997.00/7.30 per mark.

The June LIFFE future was 107 basis points in the red at 125.74 and brokers noted that earlier implied volatitity on BTP futures was heading to around nine percent amid expectations that Btps were in for a major decline.

The November 2006 Btp ended 94 basis points down at 101.56, yielding 7.65 percent and with a spread over the benchmark bund of 197 basis points. The most traded July 2006 Btp was 95 basis points lower at 106.48.
"For the June future the main support is 125.00," one broker said. "It's still nearly 80 ticks below the market and it should hold."

"The market hasn't been busy because you can hardly find buyers. We're waiting for new input. The currency is under a bit of pressure but above 1,000 it would be under more pressure," one broker said. The Bank of Italy was spotted checking rates in the 996 area earlier, athough dealers said it had not dealt.

The government is expected to unveil a mini-budget in coming weeks but the market is waiting to see what it can come up with given the hard stance of key ally Communist Refoundation on no new taxes or spending cuts.
